sections.h2: Which Houston County office to call
sections.html:
Three groups share the job here: the Tax Commissioner, the Tax Assessors and the three city offices. Collections happen at a Warner Robins office and a Perry office. Valuation and homestead filings happen in Perry. The assessors never send out bills.

Who answers what in Houston County

County bill and paymentsTax Commissioner, 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, Warner Robins, GA 31088(478) 542-2110
County bill and payments, PerryTax Commissioner, 201 Perry Parkway, Perry, GA 31069(478) 218-4940
Real property value and exemptionsTax Assessors, 201 Perry Parkway, Perry(478) 218-4750
Personal property returnsTax Assessors, Personal Property Department(478) 218-4760
City taxes: Warner Robins, Perry, CentervilleEach city's own office(478) 929-1148; (478) 988-2740; (478) 953-4734

Both commissioner offices open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. The county's pay-and-search portal lets you look up taxes online and adds a convenience fee to each payment.

Houston County has 178,214 people as of July 2025, an 8.9% rise over the April 2020 base. Robins Air Force Base is the largest employer, and sellers in Perry, Warner Robins and Centerville can expect base-connected buyers. The county holds 74,635 housing units and permitted 1,218 more in 2025. Workers travel 22.8 minutes on average.

  • Typical owner-occupied house: $219,800.
  • Homeowners occupy 66.9% of housing, so roughly a third of households rent.
  • Typical monthly rent: $1,208.
  • Typical household income: $80,698.

If you rented a house out before listing it, check whether the homestead exemption still applies. The exemption covers property you own and occupy as a legal residence.

A house that sits near the base can draw buyers who plan around a military move date, and they often want a fast closing. Tax payoffs and homestead questions are easiest to settle before such a buyer is under contract.

sections.h2: How the taxable value is set
sections.html:
Fair market value is pinned to January 1, and the taxable amount is assessed value, set by law at 40% of it. A mill is $1.00 for every $1,000 of assessed value. Whenever the Board of Tax Assessors alters a value from last year, or from the figure an owner returned, it must mail a notice.

Real property returns on form PT-50R, plus applications for conservation use, exempt status and similar programs, must be mailed with a US postmark on or before April 1. Personal property returns share that date and are taken by mail only, with forms sent in January to anyone who owns a boat, an aircraft or a business. Call (478) 218-4750 about real estate. Parcel records are searchable on the county's qpublic site.

A seller wondering whether a city levy was paid must call Warner Robins, Perry or Centerville directly, since the assessors do not bill. Confirmation of county and school tax comes from the commissioner.

Check the value on your most recent notice against the house as it is today. Finished basements, added rooms and outbuildings change the record, and so do demolitions. If the record is wrong, the 45 day appeal window is your chance to correct it, and the assessors' phone line is the quickest way to ask what is on file.

Submit your first application to the Tax Assessor's Office before April 1 of the year the benefit should start. Approved exemptions roll over annually. You file again only when ownership changes or you want a different exemption.

The statewide standard exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value, and some counties layer larger local exemptions on top. Ask the assessors at (478) 218-4750 which amounts apply to your parcel. A buyer who closes mid-year should ask how the closing date affects first-year eligibility.

To file, gather your deed information and a photo ID, and note the date you moved in. If you bought mid-year, the exemption you inherit does not transfer, so you apply in your own name. Sellers can help by telling buyers about the April 1 cutoff at the contract stage, long before closing.

Your clock is 45 days from the mailing date on the notice. The Board of Tax Assessors hears it first, re-examines its number and writes back. Unresolved appeals continue to the County Board of Equalization for a scheduled hearing and a ruling at its close. Superior court comes after that, and arbitration can replace the Board of Equalization step.

  • Permitted grounds: whether the property is taxable, the value assigned, or uniformity against similar properties.
  • Excluded: any gripe about the tax rate or amount levied.
  • Hearing officer option: limited to non-homestead real estate over $500,000.
  • Arbitration option: value only, with a certified appraisal.

If a board rules against you, a written notice of superior court appeal is due in 30 days, and unpaid prior-year tax blocks the hearing. Email property tax questions to taxquestions@houstoncountyga.gov.

Gather the notice, any photos of the house, and sale prices of nearby homes before you call. Bring them to the assessors in Perry if you want to discuss the value in person.

sections.h2: Due dates and who pays at closing
sections.html:
Read your bill or phone (478) 542-2110 for the due date. The statewide default is December 20, which a county may shift to December 1 or November 15 or replace with installments. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill is postmarked.

Title on January 1 decides who owes, and a seller leaving partway through the year gets no refund under state rules. For a Perry or Warner Robins sale, have the closing agent list county, school and city taxes on separate lines, because the cities send their own bills.

An unpaid bill can lead to a recorded lien and a later auction. Afterward, a twelve-month window lets interested parties redeem by paying the bid, subsequent taxes, special assessments and a 20% premium.

A seller with an open balance should settle it before or at closing so the title is clean.

  1. Call the commissioner in Warner Robins or Perry for the county balance.
  2. Call the city office for any city levy, since those bills come separately.
  3. Ask the assessors whether your homestead and any conservation use filing are on record.
  4. Hand all three answers to the closing agent in writing.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, so the sale can close quickly. That makes it worth having the payoff numbers ready before you accept an offer, not after.

faqs.q: Does the Houston County Tax Assessor mail my bill?
faqs.a: No, the assessors do not handle billing. Phone the commissioner at (478) 542-2110 (Warner Robins) or (478) 218-4940 (Perry) for county bills, and call your city for a city levy.

faqs.q: By when must I file a Houston County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The cutoff is April 1 of the first year you want the benefit, and the paperwork goes to the assessors. Once approved it carries forward without a new form, until the home changes hands or you ask for a different exemption.

faqs.q: How many days do I get to appeal in Houston County?
faqs.a: The window is 45 days from the day the notice was mailed, and the assessors receive the filing first. Arguing that the tax is simply too high is off the table, while taxability, value and uniformity are fair game.

faqs.q: Where can I visit the Houston County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: The Warner Robins office is on Carl Vinson Parkway (number 202), and the Perry office is on Perry Parkway (number 201). Counters stay open every weekday from half past eight until five.

faqs.q: Who pays Houston County tax when a house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is liable for the full year, and no partial-year refund exists. Ask the closing agent to break out county, school and city lines.
